title: How rate limiting protects an API
subtitle: Control bursts without confusing limits with capacity
learning_objective: Explain rate limiting and select a useful response to clients that exceed a quota.

scenes.title: ONE CLIENT, 10,000 REQUESTS
scenes.body: A retrying client or abusive caller overwhelms a service. How do you protect everyone else?

scenes.title: Limit requests over a window
scenes.body: Rate limiting caps requests or resource use per identity, key, or service. It protects shared capacity and can enforce fair usage.

scenes.title: Help well-behaved clients
scenes.body: Return clear limit information and, when known, a Retry-After hint. Clients should back off instead of immediately retrying.

scenes.question: What should a well-behaved client do after a rate-limit response?
options: Back off and respect retry guidance
scenes.explanation: Immediate retries amplify load. Backoff and retry guidance help the client recover without worsening the overload.

scenes.title: Remember this
scenes.body: Rate limits protect capacity; clear responses and client backoff make them effective.
